logline: A girl whose mother vanished into an unfathomable underground abyss descends into it with a robot boy, trading safety for depth - and every layer deeper costs something that cannot be returned.

renewal.note: A sequel film series was announced for 2026. The manga has over 22 million copies in circulation and won the 52nd Japan Cartoonists Association Award in 2023.

bollymeter.basis: Anime News Network gave Season 1 an A grade, calling it 'a nearly perfect show'; IMDb overall series 8.3; the season was broadly cited as 2017's best anime and a generational dark-fantasy debut.

pull_quotes.text: Made in Abyss is a nearly perfect show.

seasons.review_body: Made in Abyss Season 1 (Summer 2017, Kinema Citrus) is one of the most formally distinctive anime debuts of the 2010s. The show presents as a children's adventure - a round-faced girl and a white robot boy descending into wonder - and methodically reveals that the Abyss is one of the most hostile environments in contemporary fantasy fiction. ANN's Nick Creamer awarded it an A grade and called it 'a nearly perfect show,' noting that the Abyss itself functions as one of the season's primary characters. The animation quality for a debut from Kinema Citrus was cited as exceptional: backgrounds especially drew praise for their architectural detail and atmospheric weight. The Curse of the Abyss rule system introduces consequences that are physiological, irreversible, and increasingly severe - a horror design embedded inside a quest narrative. Star Crossed Anime gave it 91/100.

episode_reviews.title: The City of the Great Pit
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the Abyss with the confidence of world-building that has already worked out its internal logic completely. The city of Orth above the pit, the Cave Raider culture, the Whistle grade system, and Riko's specific circumstances as the daughter of a legendary White Whistle are all delivered without exposition-as-dialogue. The tonal tension between the show's soft visual style and the genuine danger it implies is present from the first scene.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Riko's first glimpse of Reg from the Abyss - the first signal that the series operates with a different set of rules than it initially presents.

episode_reviews.title: The Golden City
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 1 finale commits fully to the Abyss's consequence architecture: the descent costs something real in a way that no amount of preparation or heroism can prevent. The episode ends on an emotional beat that has been cited across years of anime discourse as one of the most effective season-ending choices in modern anime, setting up the Dawn of the Deep Soul arc while functioning as a complete statement about the cost of ambition.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Curse of the Abyss exacted in full - the season's thesis made physical and irreversible.

critic_note.text: The abyss itself feels like one of the show's most important characters.

bollymeter.basis: Dawn of the Deep Soul (105 min theatrical feature) bridges the first and second arcs; Rotten Tomatoes audience score 93%, described as 'an excellent movie and a great sequel to a great series.' The film adapts the Idofront arc and introduces Bondrewd as the franchise's most complex antagonist.

seasons.review_body: Dawn of the Deep Soul (January 2020, Kinema Citrus) is a 105-minute theatrical film bridging Season 1 and Season 2, adapting the Idofront arc. It introduces Bondrewd the Novel - the franchise's most philosophically complex antagonist, who treats the Curse of the Abyss as a research instrument rather than a danger. The film received a 93% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and was described as 'an excellent movie and a great sequel to a great series.' Kinema Citrus produced it at a quality level above the television seasons, and the Bondrewd confrontation is regularly cited as the franchise's finest single villain arc. The film is a non-optional bridge: Season 2 assumes its events and character consequences.
seasons.season_over_season: The Idofront arc's theatrical treatment gives Bondrewd more time than a television format would allow; essential viewing before Season 2.

bollymeter.basis: ANN critics noted the animation and music were 'elevated into masterful territory'; however the season's relentless grimness and the Zoaholic arc's content made it the franchise's most divisive season among general audiences.

pull_quotes.text: The animation and score work together to elevate this into masterful territory.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 (Summer 2022, titled The Golden City of the Scorching Sun) adapts the deepest arc in the animated series to date, set in a village at the Sixth Layer where the Curse has produced a community structured around radical self-sacrifice and bodily horror. ANN critics noted the animation and score were elevated into masterful territory in key episodes. The season is the most aesthetically extreme in the franchise and the most consistently challenged by audiences not prepared for its content escalation. Mechanical Anime Reviews and Asian Movie Pulse both cited it as one of the year's finest anime while acknowledging its deliberate difficulty. IMDb tracking held at Season 1 levels, suggesting the franchise's core audience followed the descent without significant attrition.
seasons.season_over_season: The franchise's darkest and most extreme arc; animation and score are the strongest in the series' run, but the content escalation is the most pronounced.
